races.title: State Assembly, District 36
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jeff Gonzalez
cands.bio: Republican member of the California State Assembly for District 36 since December 2024. Retired after 21 years in the U.S. Marine Corps, with combat deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan. Former pastor and small business owner. Ran unsuccessfully for Assembly District 56 in 2018. Lives in Indio.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California and Reform California endorsed him for 2026, per Ballotpedia.
California Farm Bureau, quoted on his campaign site as backing his re-election.
Imperial County Sheriff Fred Miramontes (D), quoted on his campaign site as endorsing his re-election.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Gonzalez on data centers, growth and development limits, homestead property taxes, investor or foreign land buying, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and vouchers. His campaign site mentions cutting taxes on gas and groceries, hiring more teachers and school security, and public safety, but gives no specific bills or actions on those. We could not find a specific year he moved to California. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or details of the bills he has sponsored. His campaign site says he has served on local nonprofit boards but does not name them.

local.label: Roots 90: Wikipedia says he was born in New Jersey and raised in Southern California, and he now lives in Indio.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member for District 36 since December 2024. Retired after 21 years in the Marine Corps, then worked as a pastor and now owns three small businesses. Lost a 2018 Assembly race.
qual.why: He has held legislative office for about two years, and he has run businesses and managed people. He has no documented law, policy or budget career, so he scores in the upper-middle range rather than the top band.

cands.name: Ida S. Obeso-Martinez
cands.bio: Nurse practitioner with more than 20 years in emergency, intensive care and family practice, and holds a Doctorate in Nursing Practice. Her campaign site says she is Mayor of Imperial and that she finished second in a field of six in the 2022 Imperial City Council race. Democratic candidate for Assembly District 36.

endorsements.text: California Nurses Association and Equality California are listed among her endorsements on Ballotpedia.
Her campaign site says she is backed by nurses, firefighters and Congressman Raul Ruiz. It does not list specific organizations.

cands.gaps: We found no independent record of her actions as Imperial's mayor or council member, such as votes, ordinances or budgets. Her 2022 council result and her mayoralty come only from her campaign site. We found no stated positions from her on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion or school choice. Her site's general language on public safety, schools, housing and cost of living does not address those topics specifically. She did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey. We did not find her birth year, her hometown within the Imperial Valley, or her employer.

local.label: Roots 100: Her campaign site says she was born and raised in the Imperial Valley, is a lifelong resident, and chose to raise her family in District 36.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Her campaign site says she is Mayor of the City of Imperial after a 2022 City Council run, and that she has worked 20+ years as an emergency room, intensive care and family nurse practitioner. It also says she helped secure local infrastructure and economic development funding.
qual.why: A local elected office (city council and mayor) puts her in the middle band. She has no legislative, law or budget career on the record, and the mayoral role comes only from her campaign site.
